title: Start order and health
summary: depends_on, healthchecks, and computing a start order with a topological sort.

steps.title: depends_on only orders the start
body: - db           # short form: start db first

The short form only means *"start the db container before the api container"*. Postgres needs a few seconds after its container starts before it accepts connections, so the API can still hit `Connection refused`.
To wait for **readiness**, give the dependency a **healthcheck** and use the long form:
condition: service_healthy     # wait until db's healthcheck passes
Conditions: `service_started` (the default), `service_healthy`, and `service_completed_successfully` (for a one-off job such as a migration that must finish first).

steps.prompt: The API uses the short form `depends_on: [db]` and still fails at startup with `Connection refused`. Why?
options: Short `depends_on` waits only for the db container to start, not for Postgres to accept connections
depends_on only works with `image:` services, not `build:` ones
Compose starts services in alphabetical order, ignoring depends_on
The db service needs `ports:` for the api to reach it
steps.explain: Add a healthcheck to db and `condition: service_healthy` to the API. A retry loop in the app is still wise: databases also restart in production.

steps.prompt: Make the API wait until Postgres reports healthy.
`web` depends on `api`; `api` depends on `db` (condition `service_healthy`). Arrange what Compose does on `docker compose up`.
lines: wait for db's healthcheck to pass
steps.explain: Dependencies first, all the way down; a `service_healthy` condition inserts a wait.

steps.title: Start order is a topological sort
body: Services and their `depends_on` form a **directed graph**. A valid start order lists every service after all of its dependencies: a **topological sort**. One simple way (Kahn's algorithm):
ready = services not yet started whose dependencies have all started
if ready is empty but services remain  →  there is a cycle
start one ready service (here: the alphabetically first, so the order is predictable)
web ──▶ api ──▶ db              order: db, redis, api, web
Compose rejects a cycle (`api` depends on `db`, `db` depends on `api`) with a "dependency cycle detected" error.

steps.explain: First only `db` and `redis` are ready (no dependencies); alphabetical order picks `db`. Then `redis`, then `api` (both its dependencies done), then `web`.

steps.prompt: `api` depends on `worker`, `worker` depends on `api`. What happens on `docker compose up`?
options: Compose refuses to start and reports a dependency cycle
Compose starts both at the same time
Compose starts api, then worker crashes
steps.explain: No order can satisfy both. Usually one of the dependencies is not real: the app can retry instead.

steps.title: Started is not ready: add a healthcheck
prompt: This terminal has a **real Docker Engine** with Compose. In `~/stack`, the API exits right after `docker compose up`:
the database container has **started**, but needs about 4 seconds before it accepts connections. See it:
cd ~/stack && docker compose up -d && sleep 2 && docker compose ps -a && docker compose logs api
Fix `compose.yaml` so that `db` has a healthcheck (it creates `/tmp/ready` once it accepts connections) and `api`
starts only when `db` is **healthy**. `docker compose up -d --wait` must then succeed with both services up.

checks.name: db has a healthcheck
checks.cmd: cd ~/stack && docker compose config --format json | jq -r '.services.db.healthcheck.test | join(" ")'
checks.fail: `db` has no healthcheck. `healthcheck: test: ["CMD", "test", "-f", "/tmp/ready"]` (with a short `interval`).

checks.name: api waits for service_healthy
checks.cmd: cd ~/stack && docker compose config --format json | jq -r '.services.api.depends_on.db.condition'
checks.fail: `api` does not wait for `db` to be healthy: the long form `depends_on: db: condition: service_healthy`.

checks.name: db is healthy and api is running
checks.fail: After `docker compose up -d --wait`, `db` should be `running healthy` and `api` `running`.

checks.name: the API connected
checks.cmd: cd ~/stack && docker compose logs --no-log-prefix api | tail -n 1
checks.fail: The API's last log line should say it connected.

hints: `depends_on: [db]` only waits until the db **container** has started, not until the database inside it is ready.
A healthcheck makes Docker run a probe every `interval`; the container becomes `healthy` when it passes.
Under `db`: `healthcheck: {test: ["CMD", "test", "-f", "/tmp/ready"], interval: 1s, retries: 20}`. Under `api`: `depends_on: {db: {condition: service_healthy}}`. Then `docker compose up -d --wait`.
steps.explain: `depends_on` alone orders container **starts**, which says nothing about readiness; that race is why so many stacks "work the second time". A healthcheck plus `condition: service_healthy` makes Compose wait for the real signal, and `up --wait` makes the command itself wait until everything is running and healthy, which is exactly what a CI job or a script needs before it runs tests.

steps.title: Break a dependency cycle
prompt: This terminal has a **real Docker Engine** with Compose. Someone added "the worker needs the API" to `~/stack`, and
now nothing starts: `cd ~/stack && docker compose up -d`.
Read the error, then fix the dependency that does not belong (the worker only polls a queue, it never calls the API)
without changing what the API waits for. `docker compose up -d --wait` must then start all three services.

checks.name: compose config accepts it
checks.fail: `docker compose config` still fails. It names the cycle.

checks.name: the worker no longer depends on the API
checks.cmd: cd ~/stack && docker compose config --format json | jq -r '.services.worker.depends_on // {} | keys | join(",")'

checks.name: the API still waits for a healthy db and for the worker
checks.cmd: cd ~/stack && docker compose config --format json | jq -r '.services.api.depends_on | to_entries | map(.key + "=" + .value.condition) | sort | join(" ")'
checks.fail: Keep what `api` waits for: `db` healthy and `worker` started.

checks.name: all three run
checks.fail: After `docker compose up -d --wait`, all three services should run.

hints: `docker compose config` (or `up`) prints `dependency cycle detected` and the services in the loop.
Delete the edge that is not true: the worker does not need the API.
Remove the `depends_on: [api]` block under `worker`, then `docker compose up -d --wait`.
steps.explain: Compose sorts services into a start order from `depends_on`, and a cycle has no valid order, so it refuses before starting anything. The fix is never to delete dependencies until it works: find the edge that does not describe a real need. A cycle in `depends_on` is often a hint that two services are too tightly coupled.

steps.title: Build it: started is not ready
prompt: See it happen. In the **Compose builder**, the API crashes because the database is started but not ready. Give the database a healthcheck and make the API wait for `service_healthy`, then run it.
steps.explain: `depends_on` alone only waits for the container to start. `condition: service_healthy` waits for its healthcheck, which is what an app needs.
